title: Sandboxed credential harvest page
description: Walk a cloned sign-in page that never stores or transmits what you type. Recognize harvest kits and practice reporting instead of submitting. All hosts and files are fictional training content.
learningObjectives: Spot a lookalike host on a fake portal
Recognize password + MFA collection patterns as high risk
Treat unexpected disk-image attachments as a red flag
Practice reporting instead of submitting credentials

steps.title: Open the sandbox
steps.prompt: Open the simulated portal from this lab, then return. Mark complete when you have seen the intercept / training banner.

steps.title: Claimed hostname
steps.prompt: What hostname does the training clone show for the fake portal?
steps.hint: Check the intercept panel or address chrome on the sandboxed page.

steps.title: Attachment risk
steps.prompt: The message attaches Benefits-Enrollment.iso. Why is an unexpected .iso attachment a training red flag?
choices: ISO files are always safe if the logo looks real
Disk images are a common way to deliver malware while bypassing some email filters
Only PDF attachments can be dangerous
expected: Disk images are a common way to deliver malware while bypassing some email filters

steps.title: Hash hygiene
steps.prompt: In Engine artifacts, what file name is tied to the training SHA-256 for the ISO?
steps.hint: You do not need to memorize the hash — match the attachment name in artifacts.

steps.title: Correct behavior
steps.prompt: What should a trainee do with credentials on this page?
choices: Enter a real password to test if the page works
Do not submit real secrets — report the lure and stop
Enter credentials only if MFA is requested
expected: Do not submit real secrets — report the lure and stop

hints: Typed passwords and codes are never written to storage in this app — only a training flag may be recorded.
ISO attachments in unsolicited mail are a classic initial-access pattern in awareness training.
Lookalike hosts + credential forms + MFA prompts are classic adversary-in-the-middle training signals.
